A spy guessing the basis wrongly disturbs the photon and causes errors in about a quarter of the kept bits, so they can detect her.
Using entanglement

Artur Ekert (1991) proposed using entangled pairs and a Bell test. If the Bell inequality is violated, nobody could have copied the key. This allows "device-independent" security, in which you need not even trust your own equipment. Weak points of real systems (not the theory) are the favourite targets of hackers.
Limits

Photons are lost in fibre; ranges are about a hundred kilometres without relays. QKD protects the key exchange, not the whole system, and needs authentication by other means. Many security agencies, such as the US NSA, prefer post-quantum maths over QKD for general use.
Satellites

China's Micius satellite (launched 2016) distributed entangled photons over 1,200 km (Yin et al., 2017) and enabled QKD links between Beijing and Vienna (2017). Satellites avoid fibre loss, which is why they matter for national networks.
New maths

NIST, the US standards body, published its first post-quantum standards in August 2024: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM, key exchange), 204 (ML-DSA, signatures) and 205 (SLH-DSA). These run on ordinary computers. "Harvest now, decrypt later" attacks, where spies store encrypted data to open later, make switching early important.
Evidence

QKD has run in cities and over fibre links in Europe, China and elsewhere; the Chinese network spans over 2,000 km of backbone. The security proofs are mathematical; actual attacks have exploited flawed detectors, which is why labs focus on engineering.
National Quantum Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission (NQM) in April 2023, with an outlay of about ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31, run by the Department of Science and Technology. Goals: quantum computers with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits in eight years; satellite-based secure communication between ground stations over about 2,000 km; inter-city QKD over the same range; and sensors. Four Thematic Hubs (announced in September 2024): IISc Bengaluru (computing), IIT Madras with C-DOT (communication), IIT Bombay (sensing and metrology) and IIT Delhi (materials and devices). ISRO's Space Applications Centre showed free-space QKD over 300 m in 2021. As of mid-2026, press reports of official statements describe the four hubs as working and start-ups being supported; check the latest DST or PIB release for exact figures.
Key takeaways and think-about-it

No-cloning (1982) lets spies be caught; BB84 (1984) and E91 (1991) are the key schemes. Post-quantum cryptography (NIST, August 2024) uses new maths on normal computers. NQM (April 2023): about ₹6,003.65 crore, four hubs, 2,000 km secure links as a target. Think about it Why does a spy raise the error rate in BB84? Why might a country choose post-quantum maths rather than QKD?
Quantum Gravity: The Unsolved Problem
The biggest unsolved problem

Physics rests on two great theories. General relativity (Einstein, 1915) describes gravity and the cosmos. Quantum theory describes everything else. Each works superbly in its own domain, but they speak different languages and clash where both matter: inside black holes and at the instant of the Big Bang. No one yet has a tested theory of quantum gravity. Be careful with confident claims in this area.
Smooth versus lumpy

In relativity, spacetime is a smooth stretchy sheet that matter bends. In quantum theory, everything fluctuates and comes in lumps. Treat gravity like the other forces and the calculations return infinities that cannot be removed (the theory is "non-renormalisable"). So gravity cannot simply be added as a quantum field the way light was.
Where it matters

Quantum gravity should matter at the Planck length, about 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m, and the Planck time, about 5 × 10⁻⁴⁴ s: scales named after Max Planck. This is about 10²⁰ times smaller than a proton. No accelerator can come near the energy needed. That is why there is so little data and so much debate.
Hawking's hint

In 1974 Stephen Hawking combined quantum fields with a black hole's horizon and found they glow faintly: Hawking radiation. Jacob Bekenstein (1972-73) had argued black holes have entropy proportional to horizon area. The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy hints that gravity, heat and quantum theory are linked. But radiation seems to lose the information of what fell in: the black hole information paradox, still debated. Hawking radiation has not been observed from a real black hole.
The main attempts

String theory: particles are tiny vibrating strings; needs extra dimensions; includes a graviton naturally. No experimental support yet; related ideas gave the AdS/CFT duality (Maldacena, 1997). Loop quantum gravity: space itself comes in tiny grains (Rovelli, Smolin, Ashtekar). Also untested. Others: causal sets, asymptotic safety, emergent gravity. All remain unproven; opinions differ among experts.
Can we ever check?

Ideas include tiny delays in light from distant gamma-ray bursts, gravitational waves from the early universe, and tabletop experiments. In 2017 Sougato Bose and colleagues, and independently Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral, proposed putting two tiny masses into superposition near each other and seeing if gravity entangles them. If it does, gravity must have a quantum nature. Such experiments are still under development.
What is solid

General relativity: Mercury's orbit, light bending (1919), gravitational waves (LIGO, 2015), black hole images (2019, 2022). Quantum theory: all the lessons so far. What is not known: whether gravity is quantum at all. Some physicists (e.g. Roger Penrose) suspect gravity may even cause collapse.
Myths to drop

"String theory has been proved." It has not. "Quantum gravity means anti-gravity." No. "Black holes evaporate fast." A solar-mass black hole would take about 10⁶⁷ years to evaporate by Hawking radiation.
Raychaudhuri, Ashtekar, Sen, LIGO-India

A.K. Raychaudhuri (Kolkata, 1955) derived an equation about how matter focuses under gravity; it is a basis of the Penrose-Hawking singularity theorems. Abhay Ashtekar, born in India, is a founder of loop quantum gravity. Ashoke Sen (HRI Prayagraj, now ICTS Bengaluru) is a leading string theorist. Sougato Bose (UCL, India-born) proposed the entanglement test. LIGO-India (approved 2023) will add a detector to the gravitational-wave network.
Key takeaways and think-about-it

General relativity and quantum theory conflict at the Planck scale. Hawking radiation and black hole entropy hint at a link; the information paradox is open. String theory and loop quantum gravity are untested; as of 2026 there is no accepted theory. Think about it Why can we not just test quantum gravity in an accelerator? What would it tell us if two tiny masses became entangled through gravity?
